patch_description: The baseline uses a plain or exponentially-weighted moving average, which induces a lag of roughly (W-1)/2 samples and flattens genuine trends. Key insights drawn from the context: (1) MA lag is the dominant cause of poor lag_error and false reversals; (2) weighted windows help noise but still lag. Novel approach: replace averaging with a per-window robust weighted polynomial (local quadratic) least-squares fit evaluated at the *leading edge* of the window — this extrapolates away the group delay analytically, giving near-zero phase lag. Robustness is added via iteratively reweighted least squares (Huber weights) so noise spikes don't drag the estimate. Finally, a lightweight "trend-lock" step damps spurious slope reversals: the local slope estimate is smoothed with a shrinkage factor that only weakens when evidence is strong, minimizing slope changes and false reversals while preserving true trend turning points. All processing remains causal-per-window with O(W) work per step, keeping efficiency near 1.0.
